_comment: forest_bars: Map 3's start/finish barrier, the forest's answer to rock_bars. Not a gate: a stand of living saplings and young trunks grown up out of the ground across the lane, no frame, post, lintel or cut end. Twenty-three stems rise out of the earth, the thicker ones with a buttress root or two at the foot, each leaning, bending and crossing its neighbours; eleven fork high up, nine side limbs arc out and tangle; leaves only on a few limb ends and short stems. Low poly at the source (~1,400 tris): stems are 3- to 5-gons on 3-4 rings ending in a point, limbs 3- or 4-gons, every ring radius wobbled. 10.6 x 8.5 m filling the lane's cross-section, 1.2 m through it; the stand blocks, proved by sampling 320 heights from z=0.05 to z=3.60 and measuring every clearance between drawn strand axes in plan, radii subtracted -- none exceeds 0.38. Origin at the base centre, y=0 is the ground; the stand spans local X, thickness along local Z. Textured by lib/texel.py, one tiling sheet per material class (bark, leaf, root) from forest_build.py's own painters at texel.MPT = 0.05 m per texel, box-projected; `surfaces` is 3 (sorted bark, leaf, root). Each ground stem is its own piece, capped just under the soil, with its forks, limbs, roots and leaves socketed into it. One UV set, no skin, no animation. ForestBarsCollision is ONE box (10.6 x 8.5 x 1.2 m in Godot's x, y, z), shipped as a `-boxcol` node -- ForestBarsCollision (StaticBody3D) / ForestBarsCollisionShape (CollisionShape3D, BoxShape3D size (10.6, 8.5, 1.2)); `max_tris` counts only what is drawn.
